chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, from one who heard it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'When a judge says to the one on his right and to the one on his left, "What is your view? What do you say?" — upon such a one is the curse of Allah, and the angels, and all the people. Why does he not arise from his seat and seat them in his own place?'

key_terms.أَلَّا يَقُومُ: Why does he not arise — a rhetorical sarcasm: if the judge lacks competence to decide independently, he should vacate his position
key_terms.الحاكم: The judge/ruler — one entrusted with judicial authority; in Islamic legal tradition, a judge must render independent verdicts based on evidence and law
key_terms.لعنة الله: The curse of Allah — a severe condemnation indicating divine rejection; combined here with the curse of angels and all mankind for maximum severity
key_terms.مجلسه: His seat/assembly — the judge's bench; in classical Islamic courts, the judge's seat was a symbol of juridical authority

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about a judge who consults others instead of judging independently?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) condemns a judge who defers to assessors or assistants seated beside him instead of exercising independent judicial judgment. Such a judge, rather than discharging his duty of adjudication, polls those around him for their opinions — an abrogation of the judicial authority entrusted to him. The Imam declares that Allah's curse, the curse of the angels, and the curse of all mankind fall upon such a judge, sarcastically suggesting that if he lacks the qualifications to judge independently, he should simply yield his seat entirely to those he consults.
